statement: The Cramér–Rao bound states that for any estimator $T = t(X)$ with expectation $\operatorname{E}[T] = \psi(\theta)$, its variance satisfies $\operatorname{var}(t(X)) \geq \frac{[\psi'(\theta)]^2}{I(\theta)}$, where $I(\theta)$ is the Fisher information. For an unbiased estimator of $\theta$ (where $\psi(\theta) = \theta$), the bound simplifies to $\operatorname{var}(T) \geq \frac{1}{I(\theta)}$. In the multivariate case, the covariance matrix of an estimator vector $\boldsymbol{T}(X)$ satisfies $\operatorname{cov}_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}(\boldsymbol{T}(X)) \geq \phi(\boldsymbol{\theta}) I(\boldsymbol{\theta})^{-1} \phi(\boldsymbol{\theta})^T$, which reduces to $\operatorname{cov}_{\boldsymbol{\theta}}(\boldsymbol{T}(X)) \geq I(\boldsymbol{\theta})^{-1}$ for unbiased estimators.

symbols.meaning: probability density function of X parameterized by \theta

steps.text: Define the score function $V$ using the chain rule: $V = \frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} \ln f(X;\theta) = \frac{1}{f(X;\theta)} \frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} f(X;\theta)$.

Evaluate the expectation of $V$: $\operatorname{E}(V) = \int f(x;\theta) \left[\frac{1}{f(x;\theta)} \frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} f(x;\theta)\right] dx = \frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} \int f(x;\theta) dx = \frac{\partial}{\partial \theta}(1) = 0$, swapping integration and differentiation under the regularity condition.

Compute the covariance $\operatorname{cov}(V, T)$: since $\operatorname{E}(V) = 0$, $\operatorname{cov}(V, T) = \operatorname{E}(VT) = \int t(x) \left[\frac{1}{f(x;\theta)} \frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} f(x;\theta)\right] f(x;\theta) dx = \frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} \left[\int t(x) f(x;\theta) dx\right] = \frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} \operatorname{E}(T) = \psi'(\theta)$, where integration and differentiation commute.
Square both sides and note that $\operatorname{var}(V) = I(\theta)$ to obtain $\operatorname{var}(T) \geq \frac{[\psi'(\theta)]^2}{\operatorname{var}(V)} = \frac{[\psi'(\theta)]^2}{I(\theta)}$.

assumptions.assumption: The Fisher information is always defined and finite; equivalently, for all $x$ such that $f(x;\theta) > 0$, $\frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} \log f(x;\theta)$ exists and is finite.
assumptions.breaks_when: The probability density function is not differentiable with respect to $\theta$ on its support, or the score variance integral diverges.

assumptions.assumption: Integration with respect to $x$ and differentiation with respect to $\theta$ can be interchanged in the expectation of $T(X)$ and in $\int f(x;\theta) dx$, i.e. $\frac{\partial}{\partial \theta}\left[\int T(x) f(x;\theta) dx\right] = \int T(x) \left[\frac{\partial}{\partial \theta} f(x;\theta)\right] dx$.
assumptions.breaks_when: The support of $f(x;\theta)$ depends on the parameter $\theta$ (such as $U(0, \theta)$), or the integral fails to converge uniformly.

failure_modes.signature: Estimators can achieve variance strictly smaller than the Cramér–Rao lower bound (e.g. scaling as $O(1/n^2)$ rather than $O(1/n)$).
failure_modes.cause: The support bounds of $f(x;\theta)$ depend on $\theta$, violating the regularity condition that permits interchanging differentiation and integration.

failure_modes.signature: The minimum variance unbiased (MVU) estimator exists but its variance is strictly greater than the reciprocal of Fisher information, or no unbiased estimator achieves the bound.
failure_modes.cause: No estimator achieves equality in the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality with the score function.
